newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Denktash proposes joint Cypriot police units.
newsitem.headline: Denktash proposes joint Cypriot police units.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash has proposed setting up bi-communal Cypriot police units to monitor the buffer zone on the divided island.

Speaking on Wednesday night, Denktash said such a force was necessary as the July 20 anniversary of the Turkish invasion of the island approaches, traditionally a time of tension between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities.

"I will propose the establishment of joint Greek and Turkish (Cypriot) special police units, to work together with the U.N. peacekeeping force in the buffer zone," Denktash told reporters on returning from talks on the Cyprus issue in New York.
Four Greek Cypriots and one Turkish soldier were killed last summer in violent clashes in and around the buffer zone which is normally patrolled by United Nations peacekeeping forces.
A U.N. spokesman in Cyprus said there were "signals of very tight measures on both sides" along the dividing "green line" ahead of some demonstrations planned over the next few days.
It was not clear whether the Greek Cypriot side would agree to the joint policing plan, since they do not recognise the authority or the police of the north.
Turkish troops occupied the northern third of Cyprus in 1974 in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then ruling in Athens.

Turkey said on Thursday it was sending six warships to Cyprus to mark the weekend anniversary of the invasion. Turkey's new deputy prime minister, Bulent Ecevit, who ordered the 1974 operation, is also expected to attend.
Some 30,000 troops are stationed in a Turkish Cypriot breakaway state headed by Denktash in the north of the island that only Ankara recognises.
